_comment: A third, `Sales.SaveDeal`, was RETIRED and is deliberately absent. Its entire job was to let a browser
save a deal together with its lines and payment schedule atomically -- something a client could not do
while those collections existed only as transient arrays on a SERVER entity subclass. MJ v6's Related
Record Collections put them on the generated entity instead, so the same graph now exists in the
browser and persists through `MJ.SaveEntityGraph` in one transaction. The operation had nothing left
THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES WHAT BELONGS HERE, and it is the whole lesson of that retirement: a
remote operation is an ATOMIC UNIT OF WORK, not a way to reach the server. Saving a deal is a graph
the entity layer can express, so it needs no operation. Closing one is not -- it evaluates policy,
routes to contracts and orders, stamps append-only provenance and bypasses the close lock through an
audited path, all of which must succeed or fail together. That is why these two survive and SaveDeal
Both resolve their CategoryID with @lookup against remote-operation-categories, which is why that
directory precedes this one in directoryOrder.
